P1.learning: Two legs hit but Puebla-Tigres finished 0-0. This is a high-confidence total-goals miss: the model expected at least two goals roughly three quarters of the time. Track whether low-output Puebla plus a stronger opponent creates overestimated total-goal expectations, especially when the favorite can win/control without an open game.

P2.learning: America X2 failed despite a large model-market disagreement. This adds to the J13 Guadalajara 1X miss: double-chance selections with strong model confidence can still be wrong when recent opponent form or matchup context is moving faster than the goal-history model.

P3.learning: The only winning ticket was the one the EV filter considered unattractive. This is a clean reminder that EV is an expectation across many repetitions, not a promise about one ticket. Do not validate or reject the EV filter from single-jornada outcomes.

learning: J14 improved leg accuracy to 7/9, yet only 1/3 parlays won. Parlay structure still converts a small number of leg errors into large bankroll drawdowns.
Puebla-Tigres Over 1.5 failed at 0-0 despite p_model about 74.7%; total-goal calibration around weak attacking teams deserves segmented residual review.
America X2 failed after Guadalajara 1X failed in J13. Track whether double-chance model-market disagreements are slow to absorb recent form, opponent strength, rotation or schedule context.
P3 had negative proxy EV and won 3/3, while positive-EV P1/P2 both lost. This does not invalidate EV; it shows short-run outcome and long-run decision quality are different objects.

Forced track remains below EV-disciplined control, 681.66 vs 758.95 simulated, but both are below their initial 1,000 after four/three tracked jornadas. No selector promotion or model retune authorized yet.
No V0.1R parameter changes from J14 alone. Continue accumulating residuals and exact-market audits.
